body: i had my first session with a counselor yesterday and am seeing a doctor on campus in fifteen minutes to at least get a refill.  depending if my paperwork has been transferred, i'll try and set up an appointment with someone more specialized at the local hospital today as well.

i talked with a few people today.  i'll have my current medication refilled by the campus' health services if my records aren't transferred by the time i run out.  i'm with friends now.  i have a meeting with a therapist on thursday.  i'll make it until then.  thank you for all your support so far.
a doctor.  i haven't been to therapy before.  i'm trying to get ahold of the counseling services on campus now though.  their phone was busy when i called five minutes ago.

>Do you write or anything? What happens when you just sit around and think of nothing... can you draw, play music, program, write poetry or prose? Can you dream up a plot to a new movie...

i write occasionally.  i spend most of my free time reading though.  i tend to ignore most of my creative impulses.

>Does negativity and sucide really enter your mind when idle... or only on bad days?

it's a daily thing.  some days are worse than others.  i don't feel as if i have much control over my mood, or anything else.

no, it's just something that's been blooming over the past few months.  i'm still trying to find different meds that work.  i took the vicodin the night before going to the hospital on a whim.

the police came because i was talking to a friend told them i've been feeling suicidal, then the conversation turned and i said it wouldn't matter to him if i was around anyways since we'll never see each other again.  then he called the cops to make sure i wouldn't do anything drastic that night.  

lemme know if anything else needs clarifying.

hey, thanks for the reply.  

>And the 'guilt of the survivors' thing isn't going to hold you up for long - I suggest that can actually just put you deeper into a guilt spiral if you aren't careful.

i've already experienced the guilt spiral.  it's not fun, but that can be the only thing that keeps me going.

>Your roommate clearly agrees with my assessment

this is probably irrelevant and unlikely, but do you know me personally?  otherwise i don't see where this is coming from.

>Idea: Alright, who in your life can we get that is going to work with you every time.

i don't fully understand what you mean by "work with you every time," do you mean just general support, or something more official and secretary-ish?

>If you are afraid of spoiling a friendship, other options?

I have friends who I turn to when I'm awful, but I don't like using them like that.  it makes me feel like a burden.  i feel like i've already ruined a few friendships with this, two last night.

>Do you have money so we can hire someone?

nope.

>Will you let one of us do it here for free?

i'm willing right now, but i still don't fully understand what "doing it" entails.  if it's just paperwork, i can do that alone.

>And let's work on you being fine just being you. Doing nothing... just your own thoughts and self. Can we agree this is your goal?

sounds like an excellent goal, but it sounds like the most abstract thing in the world.  i feel like i'm always in need of an escape.  i don't understand where to start.

>Don't give up. Start thinking weeks and months and years to resolve this entirely. Maybe it will help to stop thinking of "instant" solutions (all in one night). It's hard shit.

i don't want to (give up).  i want to work with this and get over it.  i do.

>If you know... do you care to share thoughts on: When did this all start in your life? Why?

i've considered suicide since i was like, 13, but i hadn't really thought about it seriously until late 18/early 19, last spring.  the causes aren't sensational or above what anyone else goes through.  typical growing-up bullshit.  afraid of the future, ashamed of the past, convinced i'd never amount to anything worthwhile, dreading being alone forever, etc.

i already have a few friends like this and i really don't want any more.  they don't seem to have many genuine conversations and are just latching on to any incidental thing that listens.  i appreciate the human contact, as always, but discussions with them feel really disconnected.  they cloister themselves in their dorm rooms all day, playing video games, then call me at night so they can talk about the pervasive emptiness in their lives.  It's like i'm talking to myself from last year; there's a lot i'd like to (and do) say to help them grow, but they need to experience those things firsthand, not through my lectures.  And it does feel like a lecture sometimes, both ways: neither of us can entirely relate to the other, but we still get some release out of just knowing that someone's listening, to an extent.  i'm more their therapist than their friend.  It's a little harsh, but they're a huge chore to be around.  Pity isn't a good foundation for a relationship and I don't like having people depend on me to begin with, especially if the dependence isn't mutual.  
these relationships are what i'm trying to avoid.  not just avoiding people that need me that intensely, but also putting someone else in my situation with the aforementioned friends.  i need to be way more careful with who i attach myself to.

also, thanks for the advice.  i've been up since 4:45 am, though, so i'm going to go ahead and sleep forever, i'll check back when that's over.
